subject: Physics
description: Sound waves, frequency, pitch, loudness, speed in media, doppler

questions.stem: SOUND requires a MEDIUM to travel because sound is:

options.option_text: A mechanical wave (needs particles to vibrate)
A transverse wave like light fully
A standing wave that doesn't move

questions.explanation: Sound = MECHANICAL LONGITUDINAL wave; needs medium (air, water, solid) — particles compress + rarefy + transmit energy. Cannot travel through VACUUM. Light + radio = ELECTROMAGNETIC waves; CAN travel through vacuum (sun's light reaches us through space). LONGITUDINAL = particles oscillate parallel to wave direction. Compare TRANSVERSE = perpendicular (light, water surface waves).

questions.stem: Speed of sound in AIR at room temperature (~20°C) is approximately:
questions.explanation: Speed of sound in dry air at 20°C = 343 m/s (~1235 km/h, ~767 mph, ~Mach 1). Increases with temperature (~0.6 m/s per °C). At 0°C = 331 m/s. WATER = ~1500 m/s (~4.4× faster than air). STEEL / IRON = ~5000 m/s (~15× faster). Speed depends on medium's elasticity + density — DENSER + MORE ELASTIC media transmit faster (counter-intuitive). Distractor 4 = speed of light (~10⁶ × faster than sound).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: PITCH of a sound is determined by its:

options.option_text: Speed of travel only through medium

questions.explanation: PITCH (high or low note) = subjective perception of FREQUENCY (Hz). High frequency → high pitch; low frequency → low pitch. Human range: ~20 Hz - 20 kHz (declines with age). Below 20 Hz = INFRASOUND (elephants, whales communicate); above 20 kHz = ULTRASOUND (bats, dolphins, medical imaging). Distractor 1 — amplitude = LOUDNESS (dB). Distractor 3 — speed determined by medium, not source. Distractor 4 — wavelength = speed/frequency; in same medium, frequency uniquely determines wavelength.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: ULTRASOUND = > 20 kHz (above human upper hearing limit). USES: medical imaging (gestational ultrasound, echocardiography); SONAR (ships, submarines, fish-finding); industrial flaw detection (NDT — non-destructive testing); cleaning (ultrasonic cleaners for jewellery, dental tools); pest repellers; ultrasonic welding. ANIMALS using ultrasound: BATS (echolocation, up to 200 kHz); DOLPHINS, WHALES; MOTHS detect bat ultrasound. INFRASOUND (< 20 Hz) — elephants, earthquakes, large explosions. Distractor 4 — light is ~10¹⁴ Hz, completely different (electromagnetic, not mechanical).

questions.stem: DOPPLER EFFECT explains why an ambulance siren sounds:

options.option_text: Higher when approaching, lower when leaving
Lower when approaching, higher when leaving

questions.explanation: DOPPLER EFFECT (1842, Christian Doppler): apparent frequency change due to relative motion between source + observer. SOURCE APPROACHING → wavefronts compressed → higher frequency → HIGHER PITCH. SOURCE RECEDING → wavefronts stretched → lower frequency → LOWER PITCH. Sudden drop as siren passes. Used in: RADAR speed guns (police), weather radar (storm tracking), medical Doppler (blood flow), astronomy (RED SHIFT — galaxies receding → expanding universe — Hubble's discovery, 1929).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: ECHO is heard distinctly when minimum reflection time is:

options.option_text: 1 second of delay from the wall
Instantly without any delay at all

questions.explanation: Echo = reflected sound heard distinctly. Minimum gap = 0.1 s (persistence of hearing) → minimum reflector distance = (speed × time)/2 = (343 × 0.1)/2 ≈ 17 m. Less than this → original + echo overlap (heard as a single, lingering sound — REVERBERATION, common in halls). Echoes used in: SONAR (ship → seabed), animal echolocation (bats, dolphins). Distractor 4 — instant reflection = no echo perceived.

questions.stem: A 'SONIC BOOM' is created when an aircraft:

options.option_text: Lands or takes off from runway
Flies at low altitude over cities
Cuts through clouds at any speed

questions.explanation: SONIC BOOM = shock wave heard as loud bang/clap when aircraft exceeds SPEED OF SOUND (Mach 1, ~343 m/s at SL). Compressed air waves accumulate at nose of aircraft; can't get out of the way → form a CONE (Mach cone) trailing behind. When the cone passes over an observer = the boom. Concorde (1976-2003) was supersonic civilian jet — banned from supersonic flight over land due to noise. Modern fighter jets (F-22, Su-30, Rafale, Tejas Mk2) routinely supersonic. Mach 2 = twice speed of sound; Mach 3 = thrice; etc.
